text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- MDs, Ontario reach agreement: Income limits eased; new doctors to be penalized for working in overserviced areas.
- Rwandan refugees trudge home: Tanzanians buffet departing guests.
- Boeing merger creates giant: Deal reached with McDonnell.
- Bacteria behind some heart disease: Findings suggest antibiotics could help prevent artherosclerosis, doctors say.
- In debt, out of politics, John Munro marches on: Once-powerful cabinet member pursues malicious-prosecution suit after trial in which all charges were thrown out.
- Fed boss seeks market balance: Greenspan wary of stock 'exuberance' as U.S. economy seems to have hit perfect pitch.
- EU spurs Irish boom: Thousands of youth flock home to work.
- Placer regroups for '97: CEO sees beyond troubled year.
- Utilities have fuel to burn, observers say.
- Indonesia hands Bre-X a second chance: Tells the Alberta firm to make a deal with Barrick on its big gold find by yearend. Failure risks the wrath of President Suharto.
- Canada may allow bigger foreign stake in telecoms.
